greek: Προσθέμενος δὲ Αβρααμ ἔλαβεν γυναῖκα, ᾗ ὄνομα Χεττουρα.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyōsep*, *and he added*, with *and took* after it. The Greek keeps the Hebrew's idiom: the participle of προστίθημι, *to put to*, and then *took*.

greek: Καὶ αὗται αἱ γενέσεις Ισαακ τοῦ υἱοῦ Αβρααμ· Αβρααμ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ισαακ.
hint: And these are the generations of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham fathered Isaac.

notes.text: The Hebrew is the same, *ʾabrāhām hôlîd ʾet-yiṣḥāq*.

hint: Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel the Syrian from Mesopotamia, sister of Laban the Syrian, as his wife.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *mippaddan ʾărām*, *from Paddan-aram*. The Greek has Mesopotamia, as at 24:10.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyeʿtar*, *and he entreated*. The Greek has δέομαι, whose first sense is *to lack, miss, stand in need of*.

hint: The Lord says: Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will be separated from your belly; one people will be stronger than the other, and the greater will serve the smaller.

hint: Her days to give birth are fulfilled, and there are twins in her belly.
